eventMetadata.context_description: Official National Weather Service forecasts for coastal Los Angeles point to a highest temperature near 78–79°F on August 19, driven by a persistent marine layer and moderate onshore flow that limits daytime heating through low stratus and a strengthening sea breeze. Recent observations at KLAX and downtown stations have shown similar upper-70s to low-80s maxima amid this pattern, consistent with climatological norms for mid-August when the Pacific high promotes cool, stable air rather than offshore warming. Trader consensus splitting probability evenly between the 78–79°F and 80–81°F bins captures remaining model uncertainty over marine-layer depth and afternoon clearing timing, while lower probabilities for 82°F+ reflect limited potential for significant warming absent a stronger high-pressure ridge or wind shift. Updated NWS guidance and morning soundings will provide the next key data points before resolution.
